transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Your Name]. Thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm in the right place for this. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is... I've been having a little trouble in the evenings. It's probably not a huge deal, but once I start eating at night, it's like... well, it feels like I can almost see myself doing it, and I'm telling myself to stop, but my hands just keep going back for more. It's a bit embarrassing to admit, honestly. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Can you tell me more about those evenings when you're eating and feel like you can't stop? Do you feel like you're losing control over how much you're eating during those times?

Well, yes, I suppose losing control is the right way to put it. I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it actually is, but... well, some evenings, I'll just start out with a few leftovers. Just a bite or two, you know? But then... I don't know, I just kind of keep going. 

I'll end up making a sandwich, and then maybe pour some cereal, have a few cookies... really just whatever snack food is sitting there in the pantry. It sounds a bit foolish for a man my age to admit, doesn't it? But before I know it, it ends up being far, far more than I would ever actually put on a plate for a normal supper. 

I'm sorry, I know it's not a very good habit. Am I explaining that right? Is that the sort of thing you were asking about?
During these times when you feel like you can't stop eating, do you keep eating even after you feel full or uncomfortable?

Well, um... I'm not entirely sure I'd say I get uncomfortable. I mean, I certainly get full, just like anyone would after a large supper, I suppose. But I haven't really noticed if I keep going until it actually hurts or anything like that. I try not to let it get *that* out of hand, if that makes sense. 

I guess I just sort of realize I've had too much and eventually wrap things up. I'm sorry, I haven't really paid very close attention to exactly how my stomach feels right in the middle of it all. I hope that's a helpful answer? Did I understand your question correctly?
When you're eating during these evenings, do you find yourself eating much more quickly than usual?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I try to just eat at my regular pace, I suppose. I don't really rush through it or shovel it in, if that's what you mean. 

I like to... well, just take my time, even when I'm, you know, having a bit too much. I hope that makes sense? I'm not trying to be difficult, I just haven't really noticed myself eating any faster than I would at a normal dinner. Is that... is that alright? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Before these evening eating episodes happen, do you usually feel stressed, anxious, sad, or upset?

Oh, um... no, I don't believe so. I mean, my life is really quite fine. Work can be busy, naturally, managing the projects and the team and all, but I wouldn't say I feel overly stressed or sad when I get home. I'm usually just... well, just having a regular, quiet evening, you know? 

I certainly don't feel upset or anxious before I start snacking. I hope that doesn't make my habit seem even more foolish... I know some folks eat when they're feeling down, but I think I just sort of... start eating without a very good excuse. 

I'm sorry, I hope that's an alright answer? I don't want to mislead you, I just haven't noticed any bad moods like that beforehand. Am I giving you the kind of information you need?
Do you ever feel ashamed or guilty about how much you eat during these evenings, or do you usually eat this way when you're alone?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I feel *ashamed*, really. I mean, it's just a bit of extra snacking, isn't it? Nothing to be terribly guilty over, I don't think. I suppose I do prefer to have my evenings to myself, just to unwind and relax in my own space. 

My wife is usually out with her book club or visiting our daughter on those nights anyway, so it just works out that I'm on my own. It's not like I'm hiding it or anything like that, it's just... well, it's just how the schedule falls. 

I hope that doesn't sound like I'm being sneaky? I just enjoy a quiet house and a bit of a treat, you know? I really hope I'm answering this the right way for you... is that the sort of detail you were looking for?
When you're having these evenings where you eat more than you plan, does it happen all in one sitting or over a long stretch of time?

Oh, well, let me think... I suppose it's more spread out, really. Over a longer stretch, I mean. I might have a little something when I first sit down, and then maybe a bit more later on while I'm looking over some blueprints or just watching a program. 

It's certainly not all at once in one big sitting—I wouldn't do that. It's just... grazing, I guess you'd call it? Just over the course of the night. I haven't really kept a strict eye on the clock, to be perfectly honest, so I can't give you an exact timeframe. 

I hope that's a satisfactory answer for you? I'm trying my best to remember how it usually goes. Does that help clarify things for your notes?
Do you usually feel physically hungry when you start eating during these evening episodes, or do you sometimes start eating even when you're not really hungry?

Oh, um... well, I suppose I must be at least a little hungry when I start. I mean, I usually work up quite an appetite during the day, dealing with the contractors and looking over the site plans and all that. 

I haven't really stopped to, you know, measure exactly how empty my stomach is beforehand. But I certainly wouldn't say I just eat for absolutely no reason at all. That would be rather... well, a bit gluttonous, wouldn't it? I just feel a bit peckish and decide to have a normal evening snack. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm sorry I can't be more precise about my exact hunger levels. I just assume it's a regular appetite. Is that... is that the sort of thing you were asking?
Do you ever find yourself eating until you feel uncomfortably full or even to the point of physical discomfort during these evening episodes?

Oh, goodness no, I wouldn't say uncomfortably full. I mean, maybe just pleasantly satisfied, like anyone would be after a good meal or a nice snack. 

I certainly don't gorge myself until I'm in pain or anything drastic like that. I just eat until I feel... well, until I feel done, I suppose. Sometimes I might feel a little heavy if I've had something rich, but it's nothing out of the ordinary. 

I try to be sensible about it, you know? I hope that's what you were looking to hear. I'm not doing anything too extreme, am I?
During these evening eating episodes, do you ever eat a much larger amount of food than most people would eat in a short period of time, like within a couple of hours?

Well, um... I suppose it might seem like a bit much if you laid it all out at once. But it's not like I'm sitting down to a feast, you understand? 

Sometimes, well, I might start with some leftovers from dinner. And then, you know, I might make a sandwich or two... and perhaps have a bowl of cereal. And then maybe some cookies, or whatever snack foods happen to be sitting in the pantry. 

When you add it all up, I suppose... well, I guess it is more than I'd ever put on a plate for a normal supper. But it just sort of happens gradually, you know? It doesn't feel like I'm eating a massive amount all at once. I'm just having a little bit of this and a little bit of that. 

I hope that doesn't sound too terrible? I'm just trying to be honest with you about how it goes. Is that the kind of information you need?
Do you ever eat in secret or feel like you need to hide your eating from others because you're embarrassed by how much or how often you eat?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I certainly don't sneak around my own house or anything like that. That would be a bit... well, a bit unseemly for a man my age, wouldn't it? 

I usually just have my snacks right there in the kitchen or the den. I suppose my wife might be in the other room reading or watching television, so she's not always standing right over me, but I'm definitely not deliberately hiding it from her. I wouldn't want you to think I'm being deceitful or sneaking food into the garage or anything drastic. 

I just eat openly, like anyone else winding down for the evening. I mean, I might not announce every time I go to the pantry, but it's not a secret. Does that... does that sound alright to you? I really do try to keep things above board.
During these evening eating times, do you ever feel like you can't stop eating or control what you're eating, even if you wanted to?

Well, um... I suppose that is actually sort of what brings me in to see you. It's a bit embarrassing to admit, to be perfectly honest. 

I wouldn't say I completely lose my mind or anything drastic like that, but... well, sometimes once I start eating at night, it's almost like I can just see myself doing it. In my head, I'm telling myself, 'Alright, that's enough now, time to stop,' but... my hands just sort of keep going back for more. 

It's just a silly habit, really, getting a bit carried away, you know? I really do try to keep a handle on things most of the time. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it the way you need me to.
Has this eating habit caused you any real distress or affected your daily life in any way?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's caused any *real* distress, not in a major way. I mean, I'm still going to work every day, managing my team at the firm just fine. I haven't let my basic responsibilities slip, you know? I'm very diligent about all of that.

But, I suppose... well, if I'm being completely open with you... it has made me a little hesitant about social things lately. My wife and I used to go to the theater quite a bit, and we have a walking club we're involved with. But recently, I've found myself making excuses to stay home. 

It's just... well, I feel a bit foolish saying it, but I worry about how I look to the others. I feel a bit ashamed, I suppose, like maybe they'll look at me and think I don't have any discipline or self-control. It's silly, I know. I just get so preoccupied with it that it's easier to just stay in. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound terribly vain or overly sensitive? I'm just trying to give you the full picture. Is that the sort of thing you were asking about?
When you're eating more than you plan during these evenings, does it usually happen within a short window of time, like a couple of hours, or does it stretch out over a much longer part of the night?

Well, um... I suppose it's mostly over a couple of hours, really. Usually right after supper and before I turn in for the night. 

I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I'm completely gorging myself or anything terribly dramatic. It's just... well, some evenings I'll start by finishing off a bit of leftovers, you know, just tidying up the kitchen. But then I might make a sandwich or two, and maybe have a bowl of cereal... and then perhaps some cookies or whatever snack foods are sitting there in the pantry. 

When I look back on it, I suppose it ends up being far more than I would ever put on a plate for a normal, sit-down supper. It just sort of adds up quickly in that short window of time. 

I feel a bit foolish laying it all out like that. I hope you don't think I'm completely out of control or anything. It's just a bad habit I've fallen into, really. Does that answer your question alright? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right sort of details.
During these evening eating episodes, do you find yourself eating much more rapidly than usual, like eating faster than you normally would during a regular meal?

Well, um... I wouldn't say I'm eating frantically or anything like that. I'm certainly not shoveling food in, you know? I try to keep things quite civilized. 

I suppose... well, maybe I do eat a bit quicker than I would if I were sitting down at a nice restaurant with my wife. When you're just standing in the kitchen, tidying up and snacking, it's easy to just sort of... take bites a little faster, without really pausing to chat or enjoy the atmosphere. 

But I certainly wouldn't call it rapid or anything alarming. Just a bit more hurried than a proper sit-down meal, perhaps. Is that the sort of thing you're asking about? I just want to be sure I'm not making it sound worse than it actually is.
